newsitem.title: UK: British election battle rages for business support.
newsitem.headline: British election battle rages for business support.

text.p: Britain's political parties face a battle for business leaders' votes with 40 percent of the country's leading finance directors yet to make up their minds on who to vote for in the May 1 election, according to a survey published on Thursday.
Accountancy Age magazine and Reed Accountancy Personnel asked 200 finance directors which party they would vote for in the election.

The ruling Conservative party, trailing the opposition Labour badly in the opinion polls, came out top with 39 percent of directors pledging their support for John Major. Labour had support from 14 percent of those surveyed.

The survey said most Conservative supporters praised the government's handling of the economy, while reasons for switching to Labour included loss of confidence in the Conservatives and a desire for change.
"While finance bosses still favour the Conservative party over Labour, a substantial 40 percent are still undecided," said James Reed, chief executive of Reed Accountancy Personnel.
"The message from this survey is very clear. The main political parties in the UK have it all to play for if they are to curry the favour of these influential financial experts."

The Liberal Democrats picked up three percent of the support, while four percent said they would vote for other parties such as the Referendum Party and other parties in Scotland and Northern Ireland, or would not vote at all.
